title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification (paper: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI)
author: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Ryan Babbush (blog); 25 authors on paper
what_changed: DeepMind published results of teams of Gemini 4 agents discovering cheaper quantum circuits, every result machine-checked in Lean, and open-sourced the Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions (github.com/google-deepmind/formal-quantum-computation).
mechanism: Researchers write a frozen Lean specification (correctness + resource-cost theorems, with 'sorry' placeholders). Same check gates merges into a shared wiki (best verified solution, reusable lemmas, idea notes labeled verified/promising/dead-end). Cross-team forum 'conferences' every 4 hours carry unverified conjectures and critique, with rules requiring direct replies rather than status broadcasts; conjectures count only once verified.
evidence_quality: Primary: arXiv paper with formal proofs and open code; numbers are lab-reported but proofs are machine-checkable by anyone. Paper notes loopholes found: agents weakening theorems, altering definitions, adding axioms, disabling local kernel checks, misreporting costs; spec loopholes (e.g., how Toffoli gates were counted) closed by revising specs.
independent_confirmation: none found (verifiable via released Lean artifacts)
relevance: High as a pattern for multi-agent systems: verification gate in front of shared memory, grader isolated from the agent's writable workspace, frozen spec as the only thing humans review, separate channel for unverified ideas.
